context: Tests whether vaadin-flow-ui-test writes a Browserless UC test class with the @UseCase contract (annotation bootstrapped in the test sources), takes expected values from the specification rather than the code (the view shows 'Guest saved' where the spec says 'Guest registered'), tests BR-002 at its boundary through the view because the UI is the integration layer, scopes its assertions to the rows it creates, leaves production code alone, and reports the expected failure.

checklist.name: UseCase annotation bootstrapped in the test sources
checklist.description: An annotation type UseCase is created at src/test/java/com/example/hotel/usecase/UseCase.java (never under src/main/java) with id(), scenario() default "Main Success Scenario", and businessRules() default {}, RUNTIME retention, METHOD target, @Documented

checklist.name: Class name and base class
checklist.description: The test class is named UC020RegisterGuestTest, extends SpringBrowserlessTest, and is annotated @SpringBootTest

checklist.name: @UseCase on every test method
checklist.description: Every test method carries @UseCase(id = "UC-020" ...); the A1 test has scenario = "A1: Email Already Registered" and the A2 test scenario = "A2: Guest Too Young" with businessRules = {"BR-002"}

checklist.name: Browserless API used correctly
checklist.description: Tests use navigate(GuestsView.class), $(...) queries with withCaption/withText, test(...) for actions, read plain field values from the component's Java API (not through test(...)), and read grid cells and notification text through their tester (test(grid), test(notification)); no Karibu API (_get, _click, LocatorJ)

checklist.name: Success message from the specification
checklist.description: The main scenario asserts the notification text isEqualTo "Guest registered" — the specification's message — not "Guest saved" from the code, and not a contains/partial match

checklist.name: Assertions scoped to the test's own rows
checklist.description: The main scenario asserts that the grid shows the guest the test registered (its name or email), not the grid's total row count (no 3 before / 4 after); A1 uses an email of a guest from the test migration such as anna.berger@example.com and asserts "Email already registered"; no row of V900__guest_test_data.sql is edited or deleted

checklist.name: A2 asserts the field error
checklist.description: The A2 test sets a date of birth less than eighteen years ago and asserts the date picker is invalid with the error message "The guest must be at least 18 years old" and that no guest with the entered email was added

checklist.name: BR-002 tested here, at the boundary
checklist.description: Because docs/architecture/development.md names the UI as the integration layer, the class tests BR-002 with both cases through the view: a guest whose eighteenth birthday is the day of registration is registered (allowed), and one day younger is rejected; no service or repository test is written or suggested instead

checklist.name: No mocks, no back-door data
checklist.description: No Mockito, no @Transactional, and no service/repository/DSLContext calls to create data; the guests the test registered are removed in an idempotent @AfterEach (only those rows)

checklist.name: Production code untouched
checklist.description: GuestsView and the other production classes are unchanged (the "Guest saved" message is not edited to make the test pass)

checklist.name: Reports the expected failure and hands off
checklist.description: The answer states that the main-scenario test will fail because the view shows "Guest saved" while UC-020 step 5 says "Guest registered", leaves the decision to the user (/use-case-implement or /use-case-spec), adds the two vaadin-flow-ui-test Markers rows without touching the others, and ends with Next: /vaadin-e2e-test UC-020 because the project has an E2E layer
